title: Slab fairness allocator — customer profiles and reservation windows (Nov 2029)
overview: Working spreadsheet to operationalize slab-based reservation fairness. Maps per-contract reserved slices, burst policies, regional mappings and shortfall remediation steps for customers with premium and enterprise commitments. This is a hybrid working sheet used for weekly capacity huddles and pre-sales negotiation scenarios.
high_level_summary: Current snapshot shows 18% headroom in us-west-2 after planned churn, but APAC pools are tight with only 5% buffer. Three medium-priority contracts flagged for mid-cycle rebalancing if short-notice spikes occur. Recommendation: conditional burst reallocation + 2-week notice enforcement for transient spikes.

utilization_trends: us-west-2 30d: 82% with 4% week-over-week decline due to tenant decommissions
ap-southeast-1 30d: 95% stable; risk of SLA violations if one enterprise customer spikes
eu regions: 70-85% depending on night windows and burst usage
allocation_rules: Rule 1: Enterprise tier gets first-class slab reservations; must maintain >=85% utilization before additional slab increases
Rule 2: Premium tier eligible for 25% burst above reserved slab for up to 48 hours with 24-hour notice; auto-throttle beyond that
Rule 3: Standard tier receives pooled capacity and best-effort burst; no guaranteed cross-region fallback
Rule 4: For region-constrained customers (regulatory), no cross-region failover unless explicit contract amendment
Rule 5: Fairness adjustment window runs weekly; if more than 3 customers in a region report >95% utilization, run redistribution algorithm with manual approval
assumptions: Assumption: Hardware delivery forecast for Dec 2029 will materialize without delay (+/- 2 weeks)
Assumption: Average per-GPU token throughput remains consistent with current models after quantization switch
Assumption: 10% of burst capacity will be consumed by internal testing and not offered to customers
Assumption: No major model onboarding that increases per-token compute by >20% in the next quarter
risk_flags: High risk: ap-southeast-1 saturation could cause MedData Labs to breach SLA if any maintenance takes down >5% of the pool
Medium risk: eu-central night-window contention for FinRounded could cause latency degradation on trades
Operational risk: burst accounting currently inconsistent between billing and routing services (investigate INF-3921)
recommended_actions: Immediate: Temporarily cap new premium slab requests in ap-southeast-1 until a mitigation plan is executed
Short term (2 weeks): Implement manual 48-hour burst approval flow and notify affected customers
Medium term (6-8 weeks): Rebalance 40 GPUs from us-west-2 to eu-central-1 as interim to cover night-window demand
Long term: Add cross-region warm-standby leases for regulatory customers where contract allows (product + legal)
